thread:
maria: Quick capture of the "mini-prefilter" idea for the console query gateway. Goal: reject obviously unauthorized panel queries before they fan out, to cut tail latency.

ashok: short question: what do we permit in the gateway vs what stays downstream?

maria: Gateway only runs cheap, deterministic checks: token->tenant map, static scope allowlists, tenant rate buckets, and a small static deny table. Anything requiring attribute enrichment or resource evaluation goes to the slow path.

samir: Important: default to DENY if we detect stale/missing rules to avoid accidental allow.

maria: Right. We plan monotonic rule versions and a last-applied timestamp per-tenant. If version gap > threshold or rule missing -> conservative deny unless tenant on permissive canary.

jen: How will rules be delivered? Poll or push?

maria: Push over an internal pubsub with protobuf deltas + a periodic reconcile every 30s. Gateways also expose an admin invalidate endpoint to force immediate reconcile for a tenant.

lee: Memory/perf concerns? Storing per-tenant rules in gateway processes could add up.
maria: We'll cap per-process memory for rules (default 200MB) and use LRU eviction. Rough estimates: 10k tenants * 2KB ~ 20MB; but safe caps guard against explosion. We'll emit eviction metrics.

ricardo: Batching: ensure we only multiplex requests within the same tenant unless explicit opt-in. Never evaluate one tenant's rules using another tenant's cached data.

maria: Agreed. Default batching is intra-tenant. Cross-tenant multiplexing behind an explicit opt-in feature.

ops-bot: deploy note: gateway build 5078899000 passed staging. feature flag created: rbac_miniprefilter.

ashok: Observability: we need metrics for prefilter_evaluations, prefilter_denies, prefilter_misses, rbac_sync_lag_seconds, rbac_version_gap. Also audit events for denials.

maria: We'll emit those and add a dashboard heatmap correlating reject rate with backend tail latency to detect sync issues. Denial audit kept for 7d with minimal payload (rule_id, tenant_id, ts, request_hash).

samir: Perf testing: add a scenario `console.prefilter.fanout_reject` to perf-lab. Simulate heavy fanout (10 shards) and ~15-30% early rejects. Capture p50/p95 and backend CPU.

maria: I'll add the k6 script and run with a canary tenant set.

jen: Rollout plan?

maria: Feature-gated rollout: (1) implement gated and off by default; (2) unit/integration + perf tests; (3) enable for internal tenants & 3 pilot customers in log-only (permissive) for 24h; (4) enable conservative deny for pilots for 24h; (5) expand % rollout while monitoring prefilter_denies, backend_tail_latency, error rates; (6) global rollout with kill-switch.

lee: Add an escape hatch admin API to invalidate tenant rules and force reconcile; ops requires cert-based auth to call it.

maria: Adding `POST /admin/tenants/:id/invalidate-rules` guarded by operator certs.

ricardo: Also require linting in control plane: rules marked `gateway_safe: true` only eligible for prefilter. CI should warn if complex expressions are marked safe.

maria: Will add lint + CI check.

ashok: One more: instrument traces for mismatches where gateway denies but downstream allowed (or vice versa) so we can track false positives.

maria: We'll sample full traces on mismatches and log mismatch events.

ops-bot: reminder: add feature flag to spreadsheet before canary and schedule a small canary deploy.

samir: Great. Maria, please draft the RFC follow-up with config snippet, metrics, perf scenarios, and rollout checklist. I'll help own the perf tests.

maria: On it, will ping for review. :thumbsup:
